mainText: This is Dose of Good for Monday, November 23. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Otters return to Kuala Lumpur as its river is cleaned up. Smooth-coated otters are increasingly seen along the Klang River, which improved from 'severely polluted' to 'moderately polluted'. Hundreds of garbage traps and solar-powered interceptors have removed tens of thousands of tonnes of waste. About 25 otters live in a nearby forest. Second: Vehicle robberies in Brazil fall 22% to the lowest level since 2019. From January to October 2026 there were 67,174 vehicle robberies, down from 86,112 in the same period of 2025. Compared with 2019 the drop is 57.7%, and October was the lowest in the series. The data come from the Ministry of Justice, covering all 27 states. Third: Injured koalas can now be treated without leaving their island. Sick koalas from North Stradbroke Island used to be sent to the mainland and could not return because of disease risk. A new veterinary foundation on the island now offers round-the-clock care. A rescued joey is gaining weight and is expected to go back to the wild near her home. Fourth: Genome of Jonathan, the 194-year-old tortoise, reveals longevity secrets. Scientists identified 287 genetic variants linked to protection against ageing in the oldest known living land animal. They involve DNA repair, inflammation and cancer suppression, and his epigenome resembles that of younger tortoises. Applying this to humans needs more research. Fifth: Newer generations reach old age with better memory. A study of about 219,000 people in Nature Medicine found those born after 1950 show slower cognitive decline. The authors link this to roughly 13% lower dementia risk per decade in Europe and the US, likely thanks to better living conditions and education. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
